page: Amazon Web Services t8i.medium is a burstable general-purpose instance managed via the AWS Nitro System hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel CPU operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, providing 2 vCPUs distributed across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains zero GPUs and does not come bundled with local instance storage, requiring remote storage solutions for persistent data. The network configuration reflects a baseline bandwidth rating of 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

The CPU operates under a burstable resource allocation model, balancing resource access for workloads characterized by low average processing requirements that occasionally require peak throughput. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides a standard memory footprint for smaller cloud infrastructure tasks. Because the baseline network throughput is rated at 0 Gbps and physical core count is limited to one, continuous heavy traffic or non-stop intensive compute tasks will face architectural constraints compared to non-burstable hardware profiles.

Given its resource sizing and burstable execution model, AWS t8i.medium delivers efficient resource consumption for low-intensity operations. It is well suited for light general-purpose workloads, microservices, small development and test environments, background staging tasks, and internal utilities that operate within burst allowances.
description: Amazon Web Services t8i.medium is a general-purpose, burstable cloud instance based on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, it features 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, coupled with 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core). The instance includes zero GPUs and provides no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage for data persistence. Its network profile lists a 0 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and it includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The burstable CPU design allows the instance to accumulate credits during low utilization and burst to higher performance when needed. This hardware profile provides a cost-effective operational footprint for entry-level workloads, making AWS t8i.medium appropriate for microservices, lightweight web utilities, testing environments, and non-continuous backend processing.
